header.sector: Consumer electronics and devices (PCs, notebooks, phones, displays)
header.title: Rising component costs threaten 2027 notebook shipments and brand margins

s01_bottom_line.text: TrendForce projects a low-single-digit 2027 notebook shipment decline, which could deepen to high-single-digit if elevated CPU/DRAM costs are fully passed to consumers; CPU, DRAM and SSD were ~68% of BOM for a US$900 notebook in 3Q26. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩

The focus of the 2027 notebook market will shift from component availability to whether consumers can absorb higher prices, with brands' ability to balance pricing, specs, supply and profitability being critical. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Notebook brands face a margin-vs-volume squeeze in 2027 that could pressure both unit shipments and gross margins, but the article does not quantify the earnings effect on any named company.

items.text: If DRAM and CPU prices stay elevated and costs are passed to consumers, the full-year shipment decline could reach the high-single-digit range. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
For a mainstream notebook with a US$900 MSRP, CPU, DRAM, and SSD accounted for approximately 68% of BOM cost in 3Q26. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Global notebook shipments are projected to decline by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
If brands mitigate retail price impact via mix/spec adjustment and cost absorption, the shipment decline could remain low-single-digit. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
DRAM supply is likely to stay tight in 2027 as AI servers absorb advanced-process capacity, limiting PC DRAM supply growth.
Replacement demand momentum is likely to weaken in periods after 2026 because some purchases were pulled forward
